title: Suns streak to top, while Wolves and Bulls make Top-10 appearances
heading: 2006-07 Power Rankings: Week 6
author: Marc Stein

rankings.summaryHtml: Five straight double-doubles for Nash, seven in eight games for Amare and three seasons in a row that Suns have had a win streak of at least 10 games. Ho hum.
rankings.summaryText: Five straight double-doubles for Nash, seven in eight games for Amare and three seasons in a row that Suns have had a win streak of at least 10 games. Ho hum.

rankings.summaryHtml: Top spot was all theirs if Spurs had handled Lakers. The consolation: Manu is back and, easing into it after a back injury, has scored 45 points in his last 44 minutes.
rankings.summaryText: Top spot was all theirs if Spurs had handled Lakers. The consolation: Manu is back and, easing into it after a back injury, has scored 45 points in his last 44 minutes.

rankings.summaryHtml: Mavs can deal with a short stay at No. 1. What they're really after is two 20-point scorers every night. Mavs are 7-1 when that happens and 7-5 when it doesn't.

rankings.summaryHtml: To get that elusive 1,000th victory -- and make the story go away -- all Sloan needs is a Boozer double-double. Jazz are 13-1 when Boozer gets one, 2-4 when he doesn't.

rankings.summaryHtml: We repeat: Who needs a smooth training camp? Kobe's Lakers couldn't have finished their forever stay at Staples (16 of 20 games) any stronger, roughing Spurs up.

rankings.summaryHtml: You can't just gloss over losses to Bobcats and Blazers. But you also can't ignore the vintage Dee-troit Bas-ket-ball at Dallas and Orlando in a back-to-back road sweep.

rankings.summaryHtml: Rockets aren't getting too carried away with their fine start. Not with four other teams in the West playing .700 ball, Phoenix right there and T-Mac's back ailing anew.
rankings.summaryText: Rockets aren't getting too carried away with their fine start. Not with four other teams in the West playing .700 ball, Phoenix right there and T-Mac's back ailing anew.

rankings.summaryHtml: Best in the East? OK, maybe not yet. But you can live with a home L to the vets from Detroit, even in a statement game, when D-Howard turns a mere 21 that same night.

rankings.summaryHtml: The mere possibility of hooking up with AI appears to have sparked KG, judging by the two huge games he strung together (win vs. Jazz, win at Bulls) after the news broke.

rankings.summaryHtml: An easier schedule certainly helped, but it was still impressive to see Bulls respond to Headbandgate with a 7-0 burst in which they averaged (no joke) 106.4 ppg.

rankings.summaryHtml: Clips are no longer the only team without a road W after conquering Memphis. But no team that started 0-7 on the road has reached the playoffs since Suns in '96-97.

rankings.summaryHtml: Facts are facts: Cavs are 7-2 with Hughes and 5-5 without him. So they welcome a healed Hughes back excitedly, whether or not he's a perfect fit next to LeBron.

rankings.summaryHtml: Nuggets' next four are all away and all in the East. They don't mind, either, because they've been much better on the road, as Pepsi losses to Hawks and Grizz suggest.

rankings.summaryHtml: Those two no-shows in Texas were hideous, but an 0-5 skid in games decided by five points or less hurts worse, including Sunday's fall-from-ahead loss in Seattle.

rankings.summaryHtml: After the last few years, Pacers are used to big letdowns by now. But the Jackson-Carlisle blowup strangely followed Jack's first two 20-point games this season.

rankings.summaryHtml: Heat have quietly won four of their past six games, three of those coming on the road, and somehow begin the new week at No. 8 in the East. What a conference.

rankings.summaryHtml: Much, much better. Wiz throttled Dallas, won their first two roadies (in a row, even) and finally saw some consistency from Arenas (four straight games of 30-plus).

rankings.summaryHtml: More Ray Allen confusion. To go with that hard-to-believe percentage from 3-point range -- just .312 -- Sonics are 3-0 since Allen went down with an ankle problem.
